chunks: And that which has been narrated is: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Isḥāq from Jaʿfar from his father (peace be upon them both) that ʿAlī (peace be upon him) used to say:

"When the Muḥrim (person in ḥajj/iḥrām state) is compelled to [eat] game or carrion, let him eat the carrion that Allah has permitted for him." This is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because the report does not state that he is compelled to both game and carrion while being capable of accessing and consuming both. If that condition is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as referring to one who cannot find game nor is able to reach it, but is able to access the carrion; in that case, it is permissible for him to consume the carrion. As for when game is available and he is capable of it, it is not permissible for him in any case. And that which indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of iḥrām during ḥajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: What should a Muḥrim eat if compelled to choose between game and carrion?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq to clarify the hierarchy of options for a muḥrim forced to eat: carrion is preferred over game only when game is inaccessible. The commentary distinguishes between mere availability and actual accessibility, establishing that if game is within reach, carrion is not permissible, thereby refining the application of the principle of necessity (ḍarūrah).
